title: Add CULL_SOLID mode to OccluderPolygon2D for solid light occluders

milestone.title: 4.x
milestone.description: Issues and pull requests slated for an undetermined Godot 4 release.

body:
## Summary

This adds a fourth cull mode (`CULL_SOLID`) to `OccluderPolygon2D` that treats the polygon as a solid, opaque shape. When a `PointLight2D` is inside a `CULL_SOLID` polygon, its light is fully blocked in all directions. When the light is outside, shadows are cast normally (identical to `CULL_DISABLED`).

Fixes #44236
Fixes #79783
Closes godotengine/godot-proposals#1320

## The problem

When a `PointLight2D` moves inside a closed `LightOccluder2D` polygon, shadows invert: the interior lights up while the exterior goes dark. This use-case can happen for top-down 2D games with an oblique camera angle, where collider objects don't match occlusion polygons. 

This happens because the shadow buffer stores depth from the light's perspective, and when the light is inside the polygon, the nearest edges are the "wrong" faces.

None of the existing cull modes handle this:
- `CULL_DISABLED` renders both faces, shadows are inverted inside occluder
- `CULL_CLOCKWISE` / `CULL_COUNTER_CLOCKWISE` are designed for one-sided walls, not solid shapes.

This has been an open issue since 2021 and comes up frequently in top-down games where lights move through objects where the colliders don't match the occluders for stylistic reasons. 

## Approach

Before rendering shadows for each `PointLight2D`, a CPU-side point-in-polygon test checks whether the light is inside any `CULL_SOLID` occluder. If it is, the shadow buffer row is cleared to zero depth (fully occluded) and normal shadow geometry rendering is skipped.

- Polygon vertices are stored in `RendererCanvasCull::LightOccluderPolygon` alongside the existing AABB (already computed from these same vertices).
- An AABB pre-check skips the O(n) polygon test for occluders whose bounding box doesn't contain the light.
- A small edge margin (2px in local space) treats lights on or very near the polygon boundary as inside, preventing light leaks during transitions.
- Works for convex and concave polygons, any winding order.
- `DirectionalLight2D` is unaffected
- No shader changes required.

A new `light_clear_shadow()` method is added to `RendererCanvasRender` (implemented for RD, GLES3, and dummy backends) to clear a shadow buffer row without rendering geometry.

## Limitations

- The transition when a light crosses the polygon boundary is abrupt (no fade). This matches how the other cull modes behave at boundaries.
- Does **not** address the separate self-shadowing issue (#105110) where an occluder shadows its own parent sprite.

## Testing

- Unit tests cover enum round-trip, point-in-polygon with transforms, AABB pre-check, and concave polygon handling.
- Manually tested with both Metal (RD) and GLES3 renderers: light outside (normal shadows), light inside (full darkness), light crossing boundary, concave polygons, multiple occluders with mixed cull modes, directional lights, open polygons, serialization round-trip.

## AI disclosure

AI was used to assist with researching the shadow pipeline internals and drafting the implementation. The design approach, all code review, manual QA testing, edge case identification (boundary light leak), and iteration on the fix were done by me. All code has been reviewed, understood, and verified to work correctly.
